summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of chronic systolic heart failure, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and alcoholic cirrhosis was admitted for hyponatremia and hyperkalemia detected during a routine outpatient visit. Her electrolyte imbalances were attributed to a combination of torsemide, irbesartan, and sodium bicarbonate. These medications were held during admission, and she received normal saline. Her sodium improved from 123 to 131 and potassium decreased from 6.1 to 4.5. She remained euvolemic and stable. On discharge, irbesartan and sodium bicarbonate were discontinued, torsemide was changed to every other day, and amlodipine was started for blood pressure control. She was advised to continue fluid restriction, monitor daily weights, and follow up with her primary care provider and nephrologist.
